summary: DeepSeek published a release candidate for its deepseek-harness (dsh) coding-agent tool, listing new UI/agent features, performance improvements, bug fixes, and several breaking changes including removal of the SQLite session persistence backend and replacement of the Session.events API.

practices.reason: Teams building on deepseek-harness must migrate off the removed SQLite persistence backend and the replaced Session.events API before upgrading.
practices.quote: Remove the optional SQLite Session persistence backend; existing content is not deleted, so use an older version to export it

practices.reason: The bidirectional parent/child agent messaging pattern via send_message is a concrete multi-agent orchestration design worth evaluating for our own agent scaffolding.
practices.quote: Let parent Agents and continuable child Agents exchange follow-up messages through `send_message`, replacing the one-way `report` tool by @Dudu-0223
